lyrics:
Kept in a box, stained before I could read
his father's hand, then his, then mine
every measure a family creed
passed down the table, line by line

At six I asked them, plain and clear
why I came out a different way
They said, "You're not the first one here —
some batches turn out gray."

It's a recipe, not a crime
inadequate — that's the design
Older than me, every time
someone else's hand behind mine

One part silence, two parts shame
a pinch of never good enough
Nothing measured that I could blame —
and somehow I turned out rough

It's a recipe, not a crime
inadequate — that's the design
Older than me, every time
someone else's hand behind mine

Nobody signs a recipe card
Nobody claims the original sin
But someone wrote it, long before me —
and called the leftovers kin

Ring around the rosy
pocket full of posies
ashes, ashes
we all fall down

It's a recipe, not a crime
inadequate — that's the design
Older than me, every time
someone else's hand behind mine

[Verse 3 - flat, itemized]

a pinch of never good enough.

and somehow I turned out rough.

[Chorus - matter-of-fact, resigned]
It's a recipe, not a crime,
inadequate — that's the design.
Older than me, every time,
someone else's hand behind mine.

[Bridge - questioning, quiet]
Nobody signs a recipe card.
Nobody claims the original sin.
But someone wrote it, long before me —
and called the leftovers kin.

[Bridge - nursery rhyme, hushed and singsong turning unsettling]
Ring around the rosy,
pocket full of posies,
ashes, ashes,
we all fall down.

It's a recipe, not a crime,
inadequate — that's the design.
Older than me, every time,
someone else's hand behind mine.

[Outro - fading hymn]

[End]

impression.text: This track establishes a deeply nostalgic and dramatic emotional atmosphere, shifting gracefully from a sparse acoustic texture to a densely layered rock arrangement. The energy level builds steadily from a gentle, reflective opening into a powerful and anthemic feel during the soaring choruses. The production is expansive and lush, allowing the intimate piano and acoustic guitars to sit clearly beneath an emotive lead vocal before thick electric guitars and sweeping strings drastically increase the overall density of the mix. A particularly distinctive moment occurs during the bridge with an unsettling interpolation of a familiar nursery rhyme, serving as a striking musical transition into the final explosive climax.

review.review_text: The conceit here is airtight: inherited inadequacy rendered as a family recipe, "one part silence, two parts shame, a pinch of never good enough," itemized so flatly it lands harder than any wail would. Rose keeps the baritone quietly resigned through a brisk 4/4 in B major, letting the arrangement do the arguing as it climbs from fingerpicked hush into something thick and weighted by the final chorus. The masterstroke is that nursery-rhyme bridge, "ring around the rosy" turning plague-sick and unsettling right before the last swell, a trick that recalls the way Roger Waters weaponized childhood singsong. If the big finish leans a touch more anthemic than the material's cold clarity strictly needs, that's a small tax on a genuinely sharp idea. A highlight.
